linda_sales: Quick heads-up — AtlasCorp POC starts Mon. Sales asked for a compact scoping note we can share with them: success criteria, timeline (2 weeks), SDK/auth pattern, expected quotas, streaming + retries behavior, and security questionnaire owner. Can we align by EOD?
priya_solutions: I can draft the scoping doc. Key success criteria we usually propose: 1) latency under 250ms p95 for chat paths, 2) 95% match on our eval prompts vs baseline for retrieval-augmented replies, 3) stable streaming with reconnect fallback. Is that OK?
sam_engineer: Those criteria look good. For the POC infra: we can offer hosted API with a sandbox API key, throttled to 10 concurrent streams and 300 requests/minute as a starting quota. We should be explicit about token cost for the eval workload.
james_se: For SDK usage share this snippet and callout: `from redwood import RedwoodClient\nclient = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")\nresp = client.chat.stream(model="rwd-medium", prompt=my_prompt)` — mention automatic reconnect on io errors and `max_retries=3`. Also note we support both REST and streaming websockets.
priya_solutions: I'll include that. For auth flows: recommend API key for the POC. If they need SSO or enterprise creds later we escalate to Dedicated/Private. Ask them if they need request-level signed tokens (short-lived).
sec-bot: Security checklist: we can complete the standard enterprise questionnaire. Owner: @sec-bot will collect answers but need customer-specific items (data residency, BYOK, audit log retention). ETA for questionnaire draft: 48 hours if we get their completed form.
ops_oncall: On quotas — confirm what "300 req/min" means for them. Are they counting requests or tokens? For us quota = requests by route; token-based billing still applies. We should offer two options: request limit or tokens-per-minute cap.
linda_sales: Good point, ops. I'll ask Atlas if they want request caps or token caps. Also ask for expected peak concurrency and token/req estimates for 10-minute demo.
sam_engineer: Streaming behavior: if a stream drops we automatically retry and resume cached prefix where possible; fallback to non-streaming with the same model if streaming slots are saturated. Make sure to call out that resume is best-effort for connectors that preserve client-side stream IDs.
james_se: Retry policy to call out in doc: exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max attempts 3, circuit-breaker after 30s of repeated failures. For POC traffic profile we can set default `max_retries=3` but expose to them.
priya_solutions: Timeline: draft scoping + security Q by today EOD; internal review tomorrow morning; share with Atlas by tomorrow afternoon. POC run: 2 weeks — week 1 integration + basic evals, week 2 load/quality tuning and acceptance.
linda_sales: Perfect. Can someone drop a short acceptance checklist for Atlas to sign off? I want 4 bullet items we can use in the statement of work.
sam_engineer: Acceptance checklist (short):
- Integration: client successfully calls chat stream and receives tokens (sample SDK test pass)
- Performance: p95 latency <250ms on sample prompts at target concurrency
- Quality: pass eval delta threshold vs baseline on 5 curated prompts
- Stability: zero unrecoverable stream failures during a 10-minute load window
priya_solutions: I'll format that into a one-pager and attach the SDK snippet + quota options + security next steps.
sec-bot: Ping me with the customer questionnaire when you get it. I'll fill standard answers and escalate any missing control evidence.
linda_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll consolidate and send final doc to this thread before EOD. :thumbsup:
